sanskrit: tasmāt taḍāgaṃ kurvīta ārāmāṃś caiva ropayet yajec ca vividhair yajñaiḥ satyaṃ ca satataṃ vadet
english: Therefore let a man dig a reservoir, and let him plant pleasure-gardens; let him worship with sacrifices of many kinds, and let him speak the truth unfailingly.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca gārhasthyaṃ dharmam akhilaṃ prabrūhi bharatarṣabha ṛddhim āpnoti kiṃ kṛtvā manuṣya iha pārthiva
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Declare to me the whole duty of the householder, O bull of the Bhāratas; by doing what, O king, does a man attain prosperity in this world?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi purāvṛttaṃ janādhipa vāsudevasya saṃvādaṃ pṛthivyāś caiva bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this matter I shall relate to you an ancient happening, O lord of men, the dialogue of Vāsudeva and the Earth, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: saṃstūya pṛthivīṃ devīṃ vāsudevaḥ pratāpavān papraccha bharataśreṣṭha yad etat pṛcchase 'dya mām
english: Having praised the goddess Earth, the mighty Vāsudeva questioned her, O best of the Bhāratas, on the very thing you now ask of me.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca gārhasthyaṃ dharmam āśritya mayā vā madvidhena vā kim avaśyaṃ dhare kāryaṃ kiṃ vā kṛtvā sukhī bhavet
english: Vāsudeva said: For one who has taken up the householder's life, by me or by one of my kind, what, O Earth, must of necessity be done, and by doing what does a man become happy?

sanskrit: pṛthivy uvāca ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā manuṣyāś caiva mādhava ijyāś caivārcanīyāś ca yathā caivaṃ nibodha me
english: The Earth said: The seers, the ancestors, the gods, and men as well, O Mādhava, are to be worshipped with sacrifice and honored with reverence; learn from me how this is done.

sanskrit: sadā yajñena devāṃś ca ātithyena ca mānavān chandataś ca yathānityam arhān yuñjīta nityaśaḥ tena hy ṛṣigaṇāḥ prītā bhavanti madhusūdana
english: Ever the gods with sacrifice, and men with hospitality, and the worthy ones day after day according to their wish—let him serve them constantly; thereby the hosts of seers are made glad, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: nityam agniṃ paricared abhuktvā balikarma ca kuryāt tathaiva devā vai prīyante madhusūdana
english: Let him tend the sacred fire daily, and before eating perform the offering of bali; thus indeed are the gods pleased, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: kuryād aharahaḥ śrāddham annādyenodakena vā payomūlaphalair vāpi pitṝṇāṃ prītim āharan
english: Day by day let him perform the śrāddha with food, or with water, or even with milk, roots, and fruits, bringing satisfaction to the ancestors.

sanskrit: siddhānnād vaiśvadevaṃ vai kuryād agnau yathāvidhi agnīṣomaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ dhānvantaryam anantaram
english: From cooked food let him make the Vaiśvadeva offering in the fire according to rule—to Agni and Soma, to the All-Gods, and thereafter to Dhanvantari.

sanskrit: prajānāṃ pataye caiva pṛthag ghomo vidhīyate tathaiva cānupūrvyeṇa balikarma prayojayet
english: To the Lord of Creatures too a separate oblation is ordained; and in the same order let him carry out the rite of the bali-offering.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāyāṃ yamāyeha pratīcyāṃ varuṇāya ca somāya cāpy udīcyāṃ vai vāstumadhye dvijātaye
english: In the south to Yama, in the west to Varuṇa, and in the north to Soma, and in the center of the dwelling to the twice-born.

sanskrit: dhanvantareḥ prāg udīcyāṃ prācyāṃ śakrāya mādhava manor vai iti ca prāhur baliṃ dvāre gṛhasya vai marudbhyo devatābhyaś ca balim antargṛhe haret
english: To Dhanvantari in the northeast, and in the east to Śakra, O Mādhava; and to Manu, they say, the bali is offered at the door of the house; while to the Maruts and the deities he should offer the bali within the house.

sanskrit: tathaiva viśvedevebhyo balim ākāśato haret niśācarebhyo bhūtebhyo baliṃ naktaṃ tathā haret
english: Likewise to the All-Gods let him offer the bali into the open air, and to the spirits that roam by night let him offer the bali in the nighttime.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtvā baliṃ samyag dadyād bhikṣāṃ dvijātaye alābhe brāhmaṇasyāgnāv agram utkṣipya nikṣipet
english: Having duly made the bali in this way, let him give alms to the twice-born; and if no brāhmaṇa is to be found, let him take up the choicest portion and cast it into the fire.

sanskrit: yadā śrāddhaṃ pitṛbhyaś ca dātum iccheta mānavaḥ tadā paścāt prakurvīta nivṛtte śrāddhakarmaṇi
english: When a man wishes to offer a śrāddha to the ancestors, let him perform these other rites afterward, once the śrāddha-rite is concluded.

sanskrit: pitṝn saṃtarpayitvā tu baliṃ kuryād vidhānataḥ vaiśvadevaṃ tataḥ kuryāt paścād brāhmaṇavācanam
english: Having gratified the ancestors, let him perform the bali according to rule; then let him make the Vaiśvadeva offering, and after that the formal address of the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tato 'nnenāvaśeṣeṇa bhojayed atithīn api arcāpūrvaṃ mahārāja tataḥ prīṇāti mānuṣān
english: Then with the food that remains let him feed his guests as well, with worship first, O great king; thereby he gives satisfaction to men.

sanskrit: anityaṃ hi sthito yasmāt tasmād atithir ucyate
english: Because he abides only for a fleeting while, he is called atithi, the guest who keeps no fixed day.

sanskrit: ācāryasya pituś caiva sakhyur āptasya cātitheḥ idam asti gṛhe mahyam iti nityaṃ nivedayet
english: To his teacher, to his father, to a friend, and to a trusted guest, let him always announce, "This much is in my house, mine to give."

sanskrit: te yad vadeyus tat kuryād iti dharmo vidhīyate gṛhasthaḥ puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇa śiṣṭāśī ca sadā bhavet
english: Whatever they may say, that let him do—so the law is laid down; and the householder, O Kṛṣṇa, should ever eat only what remains after others are served.

sanskrit: rājartvijaṃ snātakaṃ ca guruṃ śvaśuram eva ca arcayen madhuparkeṇa parisaṃvatsaroṣitān
english: A king, a priest, a snātaka, a teacher, and a father-in-law—if they have stayed away a full year—let him honor with the madhuparka offering.

sanskrit: śvabhyaś ca śvapacebhyaś ca vayobhyaś cāvaped bhuvi vaiśvadevaṃ hi nāmaitat sāyaṃprātar vidhīyate
english: And for the dogs, for the outcastes, and for the birds let him scatter food upon the ground; this indeed is called the Vaiśvadeva rite, ordained for both evening and morning.

sanskrit: etāṃs tu dharmān gārhasthān yaḥ kuryād anasūyakaḥ sa iharddhiṃ parāṃ prāpya pretya nāke mahīyate
english: Whoever, free of grudging spirit, performs these duties of the householder, having attained the highest prosperity here, is exalted in heaven hereafter.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca iti bhūmer vacaḥ śrutvā vāsudevaḥ pratāpavān tathā cakāra satataṃ tvam apy evaṃ samācara
english: Bhīṣma said: Having heard these words of the Earth, the mighty Vāsudeva did accordingly ever after; do you too conduct yourself in this same way.

sanskrit: evaṃ gṛhasthadharmaṃ tvaṃ cetayāno narādhipa ihaloke yaśaḥ prāpya pretya svargam avāpsyasi
english: Thus mindful of the householder's duty, O ruler of men, you shall win fame in this world and, departing, shall attain heaven.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ālokadānaṃ nāmaitat kīdṛśaṃ bharatarṣabha katham etat samutpannaṃ phalaṃ cātra bravīhi me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This thing called the giving of light—of what nature is it, O bull of the Bhāratas? How did it arise, and what is its fruit? Tell me of it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam manoḥ prajāpater vādaṃ suvarṇasya ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they cite an ancient tale, the discourse of Manu the Lord of Creatures and of Suvarṇa, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tapasvī kaś cid abhavat suvarṇo nāma nāmataḥ varṇato hemavarṇaḥ sa suvarṇa iti paprathe
english: There was once an ascetic, Suvarṇa by name; golden of hue in color, he was renowned as Suvarṇa, "the gold-colored one."

sanskrit: kulaśīlaguṇopetaḥ svādhyāye ca paraṃ gataḥ bahūn svavaṃśaprabhavān samatītaḥ svakair guṇaiḥ
english: Endowed with high birth, character, and virtue, and grown supreme in the study of sacred texts, he surpassed by his own merits many who had sprung from his lineage.

sanskrit: sa kadā cin manuṃ vipro dadarśopasasarpa ca kuśalapraśnam anyonyaṃ tau ca tatra pracakratuḥ
english: On a certain day that brāhmaṇa beheld Manu and approached him, and there the two of them exchanged inquiries after one another's welfare.

sanskrit: tatas tau siddhasaṃkalpau merau kāñcanaparvate ramaṇīye śilāpṛṣṭhe sahitau saṃnyaṣīdatām
english: Then those two, whose every resolve was fulfilled, sat down together upon a delightful slab of rock on Meru, the golden mountain.

sanskrit: tatra tau kathayām āstāṃ kathā nānāvidhāśrayāḥ brahmarṣidevadaityānāṃ purāṇānāṃ mahātmanām
english: There the two conversed in tales of many a theme, concerning the brāhmaṇa-seers, the gods, and the daityas, the great-souled ones of ancient days.

sanskrit: suvarṇas tv abravīd vākyaṃ manuṃ svāyaṃbhuvaṃ prabhum hitārthaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ praśnaṃ me vaktum arhasi
english: Then Suvarṇa spoke these words to the lord Manu, the self-born: "For the good of all beings, be pleased to answer a question of mine."

sanskrit: sumanobhir yad ijyante daivatāni prajeśvara kim etat katham utpannaṃ phalayogaṃ ca śaṃsa me
english: "The deities are worshipped with flowers, O Lord of Creatures—what is this, and how did it come about? Declare to me too the fruit that attends it."

sanskrit: manur uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam śukrasya ca baleś caiva saṃvādaṃ vai samāgame
english: Manu said: On this too they cite this ancient tale, the dialogue of Śukra and Bali at their meeting.

sanskrit: baler vairocanasyeha trailokyam anuśāsataḥ samīpam ājagāmāśu śukro bhṛgukulodvahaḥ
english: To Bali, son of Virocana, while he ruled over the three worlds, there came in haste Śukra, the upholder of Bhṛgu's line.

sanskrit: tam arghyādibhir abhyarcya bhārgavaṃ so 'surādhipaḥ niṣasādāsane paścād vidhivad bhūridakṣiṇaḥ
english: Having honored that scion of Bhṛgu with the arghya and the rest, that lord of the asuras, lavish in his largesse, afterward took his seat according to rule.

sanskrit: katheyam abhavat tatra yā tvayā parikīrtitā sumanodhūpadīpānāṃ saṃpradāne phalaṃ prati
english: There arose this very topic which you have now recounted, concerning the fruit that lies in the giving of flowers, incense, and lamps.

sanskrit: tataḥ papraccha daityendraḥ kavīndraṃ praśnam uttamam sumanodhūpadīpānāṃ kiṃ phalaṃ brahmavittama pradānasya dvijaśreṣṭha tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Then the lord of the daityas put this excellent question to the chief of seers: "What is the fruit of giving flowers, incense, and lamps, O best knower of the Brahman? That, O foremost of the twice-born, be pleased to tell."

sanskrit: śukra uvāca tapaḥ pūrvaṃ samutpannaṃ dharmas tasmād anantaram etasminn antare caiva vīrudoṣadhya eva ca
english: Śukra said: Austerity arose first; from it, immediately after, came the Law; and in this same interval came the creepers and the healing herbs as well.

sanskrit: somasyātmā ca bahudhā saṃbhūtaḥ pṛthivītale amṛtaṃ ca viṣaṃ caiva yāś cānyās tulyajātayaḥ
english: And the essence of Soma came to be in manifold forms upon the face of the earth—the nectar and the poison, and those other things of like kinds.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ manasaḥ prītiṃ sadyaḥ puṣṭiṃ dadāti ca mano glapayate tīvraṃ viṣaṃ gandhena sarvaśaḥ
english: Nectar gives the mind delight and at once bestows nourishment; sharp poison wholly wearies the mind by its very smell.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ maṅgalaṃ viddhi mahad viṣam amaṅgalam oṣadhyo hy amṛtaṃ sarvaṃ viṣaṃ tejo 'gnisaṃbhavam
english: Know nectar to be auspicious, and grievous poison to be inauspicious; all healing herbs are nectar, while poison is a fiery power born of fire.

sanskrit: mano hlādayate yasmāc chriyaṃ cāpi dadhāti ha tasmāt sumanasaḥ proktā naraiḥ sukṛtakarmabhiḥ
english: Because they gladden the mind (manas) and also bestow splendor, they are called sumanasaḥ, "flowers," by men who do righteous deeds.

sanskrit: devatābhyaḥ sumanaso yo dadāti naraḥ śuciḥ tasmāt sumanasaḥ proktā yasmāt tuṣyanti devatāḥ
english: The pure man who gives flowers to the deities—because of him too they are called sumanasaḥ, since by them the deities are well pleased.

sanskrit: yaṃ yam uddiśya dīyeran devaṃ sumanasaḥ prabho maṅgalārthaṃ sa tenāsya prīto bhavati daityapa
english: To whatever god, O lord, the flowers are offered for the sake of blessing, by that gift is that god made gracious to the giver, O ruler of the daityas.

sanskrit: jñeyās tūgrāś ca saumyāś ca tejasvinyaś ca tāḥ pṛthak oṣadhyo bahuvīryāś ca bahurūpās tathaiva ca
english: But the healing herbs are to be known severally—the fierce, the gentle, and the radiant—of many potencies and of many forms as well.

sanskrit: yajñiyānāṃ ca vṛkṣāṇām ayajñiyān nibodha me āsurāṇi ca mālyāni daivatebhyo hitāni ca
english: Of the trees fit for sacrifice and of those unfit, learn from me, and of the garlands proper to the asuras and of those wholesome for the gods.

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ surāṇāṃ ca yakṣāṇāṃ ca tathā priyāḥ pitṝṇāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca kāntā yās tv anupūrvaśaḥ
english: And which are dear to the rākṣasas, the gods, and the yakṣas, and which are beloved of the ancestors and of men—all in their due order.

sanskrit: vanyā grāmyāś ceha tathā kṛṣṭoptāḥ parvatāśrayāḥ akaṇṭakāḥ kaṇṭakinyo gandharūparasānvitāḥ
english: Wild and cultivated alike, sown in tilled ground or mountain-dwelling, thornless or thorn-bearing, possessed of fragrance, form, and savor.

sanskrit: dvividho hi smṛto gandha iṣṭo 'niṣṭaś ca puṣpajaḥ iṣṭagandhāni devānāṃ puṣpāṇīti vibhāvayet
english: Twofold is the fragrance held to be that is born of flowers, the pleasant and the unpleasant; let him understand that flowers of pleasant fragrance are for the gods.

sanskrit: akaṇṭakānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ śvetaprāyāś ca varṇataḥ teṣāṃ puṣpāṇi devānām iṣṭāni satataṃ prabho
english: Of thornless trees, and those mostly white in color—their flowers are ever pleasing to the gods, O lord.

sanskrit: jalajāni ca mālyāni padmādīni ca yāni ca gandharvanāgayakṣebhyas tāni dadyād vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: And the water-born garlands, the lotuses and the like, and whatever others there are—those let the discerning man give to the gandharvas, the nāgas, and the yakṣas.

sanskrit: oṣadhyo raktapuṣpāś ca kaṭukāḥ kaṇṭakānvitāḥ śatrūṇām abhicārārtham atharvasu nidarśitāḥ
english: Herbs with red flowers, pungent and beset with thorns, are shown in the Atharvan texts to be for the working of sorcery against foes.

sanskrit: tīkṣṇavīryās tu bhūtānāṃ durālambhāḥ sakaṇṭakāḥ raktabhūyiṣṭhavarṇāś ca kṛṣṇāś caivopahārayet
english: But those of sharp potency, hard to grasp and thorny, of color mostly red, and the black ones too—let him offer to the spirits.

sanskrit: manohṛdayanandinyo vimarde madhurāś ca yāḥ cārurūpāḥ sumanaso mānuṣāṇāṃ smṛtā vibho
english: Those flowers that gladden the mind and heart, sweet when crushed and fair of form, are held to be for men, O lord.

sanskrit: na tu śmaśānasaṃbhūtā na devāyatanodbhavāḥ saṃnayet puṣṭiyukteṣu vivāheṣu rahaḥsu ca
english: But let him not bring such as have grown in cremation-grounds, nor such as have sprung up in temples of the gods, into rites of prosperity, into weddings, or into private chambers.

sanskrit: girisānuruhāḥ saumyā devānām upapādayet prokṣitābhyukṣitāḥ saumyā yathāyogaṃ yathāsmṛti
english: The gentle flowers that grow on mountain-slopes let him present to the gods, gentle and sprinkled and besprinkled with water, as is fitting and as tradition prescribes.

sanskrit: gandhena devās tuṣyanti darśanād yakṣarākṣasāḥ nāgāḥ samupabhogena tribhir etais tu mānuṣāḥ
english: By fragrance the gods are pleased, by the sight the yakṣas and rākṣasas, the nāgas by actual enjoyment; but men by all three of these.

sanskrit: sadyaḥ prīṇāti devān vai te prītā bhāvayanty uta saṃkalpasiddhā martyānām īpsitaiś ca manorathaiḥ
english: At once he gladdens the gods, and they, being gladdened, foster mortals, fulfilling their resolves and the longings of their hearts.

sanskrit: devāḥ prīṇanti satataṃ mānitā mānayanti ca avajñātāvadhūtāś ca nirdahanty adhamān narān
english: The gods are ever pleased when honored, and they honor in return; but when slighted and spurned, they burn up the basest of men.

sanskrit: ataūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi dhūpadānavidhau phalam dhūpāṃś ca vividhān sādhūn asādhūṃś ca nibodha me
english: Hereafter I shall declare the fruit in the rite of giving incense; and the manifold incenses, the good and the bad alike, learn from me.

sanskrit: niryāsaḥ saralaś caiva kṛtrimaś caiva te trayaḥ iṣṭāniṣṭo bhaved gandhas tan me vistarataḥ śṛṇu
english: The resinous, the simple, and the compounded—these are the three; their fragrance may be pleasant or unpleasant; hear this from me in detail.

sanskrit: niryāsāḥ sallakīvarjyā devānāṃ dayitās tu te gugguluḥ pravaras teṣāṃ sarveṣām iti niścayaḥ
english: The resins, save that of the sallakī tree, are dear to the gods; and of them all guggulu is the choicest—so it is settled.

sanskrit: aguruḥ sāriṇāṃ śreṣṭho yakṣarākṣasabhoginām daityānāṃ sallakījaś ca kāṅkṣito yaś ca tadvidhaḥ
english: Aloe-wood is the best of the simple kinds for the yakṣas, rākṣasas, and serpents; while the sallakī-born resin, and whatever is of that sort, is coveted by the daityas.

sanskrit: atha sarjarasādīnāṃ gandhaiḥ pārthivadāravaiḥ phāṇitāsavasaṃyuktair manuṣyāṇāṃ vidhīyate
english: Then with the fragrances of sarja-resin and the like, of earthy and woody substances, combined with treacle and fermented liquor, is the incense ordained for men.

sanskrit: devadānavabhūtānāṃ sadyas tuṣṭikaraḥ smṛtaḥ ye 'nye vaihārikās te tu mānuṣāṇām iti smṛtāḥ
english: It is held to give instant satisfaction to gods, dānavas, and spirits; but those others that serve for pleasure are reckoned to be for men.

sanskrit: ya evoktāḥ sumanasāṃ pradāne guṇahetavaḥ dhūpeṣv api parijñeyās ta eva prītivardhanāḥ
english: Those very grounds of merit that were named in the giving of flowers are to be understood in the matter of incense too; these same are what increase favor.

sanskrit: dīpadāne pravakṣyāmi phalayogam anuttamam yathā yena yadā caiva pradeyā yādṛśāś ca te
english: In the giving of lamps I shall declare the unsurpassed fruit that attends it—how, with what, and when they should be given, and of what kind they are.

sanskrit: jyotis tejaḥ prakāśaś cāpy ūrdhvagaṃ cāpi varṇyate pradānaṃ tejasāṃ tasmāt tejo vardhayate nṛṇām
english: Light, splendor, and radiance are described as ever upward-moving; therefore the giving of lights increases the splendor of men.

sanskrit: andhaṃ tamas tamisraṃ ca dakṣiṇāyanam eva ca uttarāyaṇam etasmāj jyotirdānaṃ praśasyate
english: Blind darkness and the gloom of night, and the sun's southward course; from this is the northward course; and on this account the giving of light is praised.

sanskrit: yasmād ūrdhvagam etat tu tamasaś caiva bheṣajam tasmād ūrdhvagater dātā bhaved iti viniścayaḥ
english: Because this light moves upward and is the very remedy for darkness, therefore the giver becomes one of upward course—so it is determined.

sanskrit: devās tejasvino yasmāt prabhāvantaḥ prakāśakāḥ tāmasā rākṣasāś ceti tasmād dīpaḥ pradīyate
english: Because the gods are radiant, mighty, and luminous, while the rākṣasas are of darkness, therefore the lamp is given.

sanskrit: ālokadānāc cakṣuṣmān prabhāyukto bhaven naraḥ tān dattvā nopahiṃseta na haren nopanāśayet
english: By the giving of light a man becomes keen-eyed and endowed with radiance; having given such lamps, let him not damage them, nor steal them, nor cause them to perish.

sanskrit: dīpahartā bhaved andhas tamogatir asuprabhaḥ dīpapradaḥ svargaloke dīpamālī virājate
english: The stealer of a lamp becomes blind, doomed to a dark course and of dim luster; but the giver of lamps shines forth, garlanded with lamps, in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: haviṣā prathamaḥ kalpo dvitīyas tv auṣadhīrasaiḥ vasāmedosthiniryāsair na kāryaḥ puṣṭim icchatā
english: With clarified butter is the first manner of lighting, and the second with the saps of herbs; but with fat, marrow, bone, or resinous gum it must not be done by one who desires prosperity.

sanskrit: giriprapāte gahane caityasthāne catuṣpathe dīpadātā bhaven nityaṃ ya icched bhūtim ātmanaḥ
english: At a mountain precipice, in a thicket, at a shrine, or at a crossroads, let him ever be a giver of lamps who desires his own welfare.

sanskrit: kuloddyoto viśuddhātmā prakāśatvaṃ ca gacchati jyotiṣāṃ caiva sālokyaṃ dīpadātā naraḥ sadā
english: The man who gives lamps becomes ever the lamp of his lineage, pure of soul; he attains to radiance and to dwelling in the same sphere as the luminaries.

sanskrit: balikarmasu vakṣyāmi guṇān karmaphalodayān devayakṣoraganṛṇāṃ bhūtānām atha rakṣasām
english: In the rites of bali-offering I shall declare the merits and the rising fruits of the act—for gods, yakṣas, serpents, and men, and for spirits and rākṣasas.
